items.title: SELLAS plunges premarket as $150M discounted stock offering follows positive Phase 3
items.summary: SELLAS priced an $150 million equity offering at $13 per share after announcing favorable Phase 3 leukemia survival results. Shares fell sharply in November 19 premarket trading. The financing strengthens potential development resources but creates dilution, while FDA approval and commercial execution remain uncertain.

observations.label: November 19, 07:05 AM ET premarket quote (Benzinga)
observations.value: SLS $13.66, -23.9%; preliminary quote, not a confirmed closing return; snapshots from other sources/times differ

observations.label: November 18, 21:59 ET priced offering (company)
observations.value: 11,538,462 new shares at $13/share; $150M gross proceeds before fees; underwriters' option for up to 1,730,769 additional shares; planned Nov 20 closing

observations.label: November 17 Phase 3 REGAL clinical topline (company and SEC)
observations.value: 126 participants; median overall survival 24.0 vs 14.7 months; hazard ratio 0.59, two-sided p=0.035; FDA review and approval pending

observations.label: Risks and next checks
observations.value: New-equity dilution, FDA meeting and BLA timing, full trial data, commercialization costs, US regular-session price and volume; unfavorable regulatory path or cash needs would weaken clinical-versus-financing watch

items.key_finding: A sharp SLS repricing follows discounted financing despite positive pivotal survival data; regulatory and dilution risks remain.

sources.title: SEC Form 8-K and REGAL Phase 3 data

items.title: PDD ADR rebounds sharply on earnings beat despite flat revenue
items.summary: PDD's November 19 results beat profitability expectations while revenue remained flat year over year and below consensus. Its US-listed ADR rose sharply before the open, reversing part of a sustained drawdown. Lower expenses supported profits, but transaction-service weakness and overseas regulation remain important risks.

observations.label: November 19 07:13 AM EST premarket observation
observations.value: PDD about $84.86, +9.6% before US cash open (Investing.com); intraday quote, not closing return

observations.label: November 19 company earnings release for Q3 2026
observations.value: Revenue RMB108.3B (approximately flat YoY); non-GAAP diluted EPS/ADR RMB21.04 versus approximately RMB18.54 consensus; operating profit RMB31.2B

observations.label: Balance sheet and business quality
observations.value: Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments RMB455.4B; online marketing revenue +12%, transaction services -12%; sales/marketing spending lower

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Cash-session volume and price, Temu retention and EU regulatory issues, domestic consumption, revenue mix, operating cash conversion; renewed margin erosion or weak transaction services challenge rebound

items.key_finding: A profitability surprise drove a sharp PDD premarket rebound without confirming revenue reacceleration.

sources.title: PDD Holdings official November 19 Q3 earnings release
Investing.com November 19 07:13 AM EST premarket observation

items.title: UKMTO 212 documents another engine-room tanker strike near Khasab
items.summary: UKMTO warning 212 reports a tanker hit by an unknown projectile while departing Hormuz on November 18, six nautical miles north of Khasab. The agency said the crew were safe and damage was not yet assessed. The report differs from warning 211, but the vessel identity and incremental export impact remain unverified.

observations.label: UKMTO warning 212-26 and incident time
observations.value: Attack reported for November 18 16:45 UTC (11:45 AM EST); delayed warning around 22:30 UTC (5:30 PM EST)

observations.label: Reported physical security effect
observations.value: Unknown projectile struck outbound tanker engine room 6NM north of Khasab, Oman; crew safe; damage, cargo loss and attribution unknown

observations.label: Market confirmation
observations.value: No independently verified incident-specific XLE/XOP move or additional physical oil-flow loss as of November 19 08:30 AM EST; crude trading near $92-$93 Brent in early reports

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Vessel and cargo identity, comparison with UKMTO 211, salvage and crew status, MARAD/UKMTO follow-ups, Hormuz transits, freight/insurance, Brent/WTI; stable export volumes reduce supply-impact case

items.key_finding: A further agency-reported physical tanker attack adds security risk, not verified sustained oil-export loss.

items.title: Anthropic prices record IPO as Nasdaq futures and AI-linked equities rebound
items.summary: Anthropic priced its expanded initial public offering above the marketed range, raising about $81 billion and valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion. Nasdaq futures gained around 2% early Thursday, alongside some European AI-related shares. The IPO confirms financing demand, not durable profitability or a sustained equity-market recovery.

observations.label: November 18 IPO pricing, Reuters and AP
observations.value: $83/share; approximately $81.3B offering proceeds; approximately $1.5T fully diluted valuation; expected Nasdaq debut November 19, ticker ANT

observations.label: November 19, approximately 4:01 AM EST premarket, Reuters
observations.value: Nasdaq futures up approximately 2%; European ASML, Infineon and Siemens Energy shares approximately +3% in early reporting; not closing prices

observations.label: Fundamental context
observations.value: Strong investor demand versus unproven long-term profitability, very large AI infrastructure commitments and financing sensitivity

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: ANT opening and closing prices, AI breadth, 10-year yields, hyperscaler spending and margins; weak debut or deterioration in cash generation would challenge rebound

items.key_finding: Record AI IPO fundraising lifted market sentiment without proving infrastructure economics.

sources.title: Reuters November 19: Anthropic IPO and Nasdaq futures

items.title: Riyadh PIF Tower damaged after missile threat amid regional escalation
items.summary: Saudi officials reported debris from a missile threat caused damage in Riyadh. Witness reporting carried by AP and the Financial Times identifies damage to the Public Investment Fund Tower. Attribution and any resulting energy infrastructure or export disruption are unconfirmed; the incident adds to regional security risk without proving a new oil-flow loss.

observations.label: November 19 early morning local incident
observations.value: Saudi coalition reported missile debris and material damage in Riyadh; AP and FT identified damage at PIF Tower

observations.label: Market move verification
observations.value: No independently verified incident-specific security or oil equity price move; crude approximately steady at 02:03 AM EST Reuters snapshot

observations.label: Verified physical-flow impact
observations.value: No new Saudi petroleum production, refinery or export interruption demonstrated from this incident

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Official attribution, Saudi Aramco/terminal status, Houthi attacks, Red Sea transit, MARAD/UKMTO, Brent/WTI and freight premiums; uninterrupted operations or de-escalation weaken supply impact

items.key_finding: Confirmed damage in Riyadh expands regional security risk, with no verified new oil-production loss.

sources.title: AP November 19: Damage in Riyadh and Gulf incidents
Financial Times: Saudi sovereign wealth fund headquarters damaged
